title: FLI open letter on robust and beneficial AI
description: The Future of Life Institute published an open letter, signed by many AI researchers, calling for research to make increasingly capable AI systems robust and beneficial, with an attached research priorities document.
notes: Key sentence: 'We recommend expanded research aimed at ensuring that increasingly capable AI systems are robust and beneficial: our AI systems must do what we want them to do.' DATE CAVEAT: the current FLI page header says 'Published 28 October, 2015', but the Internet Archive's earliest capture of the letter's original address, futureoflife.org/misc/open_letter, is dated 2015-01-11 00:27:47 UTC (timestamp 20150111002747) and already shows the page titled 'Research Priorities for Robust and Beneficial Artificial Intelligence: an Open Letter' with the same text; captures follow on Jan 11, 13, 15, 16 and 17, 2015. So the letter was public by 11 January 2015; the October 2015 date appears to be a later date on the rebuilt site. The exact first-publication day was not confirmed from a primary source, so the date is recorded at month precision. Archived copy: http://web.archive.org/web/20150111002747/http://futureoflife.org:80/misc/open_letter

title: Pause Giant AI Experiments letter
description: The Future of Life Institute published an open letter asking AI labs to pause training of systems more powerful than GPT-4 for at least six months.
notes: Key sentence: 'Therefore, we call on all AI labs to immediately pause for at least 6 months the training of AI systems more powerful than GPT-4. This pause should be public and verifiable, and include all key actors.' Page header: 'Published 22 March, 2023'. Signature count shown on the page at retrieval (2026-09-30): 31,810.

title: CAIS Statement on AI Risk
description: The Center for AI Safety released a one-sentence statement on extinction risk from AI, signed by leading AI scientists and the heads of major AI labs.
notes: Full statement: 'Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.' Date from the CAIS press release, 'For immediate release: May 30, 2023' (https://www.safe.ai/press-release). Early signatories listed include Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, Demis Hassabis, Sam Altman and Dario Amodei.

title: Bletchley Park AI Safety Summit and Declaration
description: The UK hosted the first AI Safety Summit at Bletchley Park on 1-2 November 2023; attending countries agreed the Bletchley Declaration on risks from frontier AI.
notes: Key sentence: 'There is potential for serious, even catastrophic, harm, either deliberate or unintentional, stemming from the most significant capabilities of these AI models.' gov.uk: 'Published 1 November 2023' (last updated 13 February 2025). Summit ran 1-2 November 2023; this one row stands for both the summit and the declaration.

title: US Executive Order 14110 on AI
description: President Biden signed Executive Order 14110, 'Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence'; it was published in the Federal Register on 1 November 2023 and revoked on 20 January 2025.
notes: Key sentence (Sec. 1): 'Artificial intelligence (AI) holds extraordinary potential for both promise and peril.' Signing date 2023-10-30, publication 2023-11-01, document 2023-24283, citation 88 FR 75191 (Federal Register API record). Revoked by EO 14148, January 20, 2025. White House archive text: https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/presidential-actions/2023/10/30/executive-order-on-the-safe-secure-and-trustworthy-development-and-use-of-artificial-intelligence/

title: Epoch: Compute trends across three eras
description: Epoch AI reported that in the deep learning era, which 'starts somewhere between 2010 and 2012', training compute of machine learning systems 'displays a doubling time of approximately 6 months', versus about 20 months before.
notes: Sevilla, Heim, Ho, Besiroglu, Hobbhahn, Villalobos, 'Compute Trends Across Three Eras of Machine Learning', published Feb 16, 2022 (updated May 2, 2022). Quoted: pre-deep-learning era 'training compute approximately follows Moore's Law, with a doubling time of approximately every 20 months'; deep learning era 'displays a doubling time of approximately 6 months'; separate large-scale models trend 'with a doubling time of about 10 months'.

title: Epoch: Algorithmic progress in language models
description: Epoch AI reported that 'the level of compute needed to achieve a given level of performance has halved roughly every 8 months, with a 95% confidence interval of 5 to 14 months.'
notes: Ho, Besiroglu, Erdil, Owen, Rahman, Guo, Atkinson, Thompson, Sevilla, 'Algorithmic progress in language models', published Mar 12, 2024.

title: Epoch: Frontier training compute grows 4-5x per year
description: Epoch AI reported that 'the compute used to train recent models grew 4-5x yearly from 2010 to May 2024.'
notes: Sevilla and Roldan, 'Training compute of frontier AI models grows by 4-5x per year', published May 28, 2024.

title: Epoch: Will we run out of data?
description: Epoch AI projected that 'if trends continue, language models will fully utilize the stock of human-generated public text between 2026 and 2032.'
notes: Villalobos, Ho, Sevilla, Besiroglu, Heim, Hobbhahn, 'Will we run out of data? Limits of LLM scaling based on human-generated data', published Jun 6, 2024.

title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol at Go
description: DeepMind's AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol, one of the world's strongest Go players, by four games to one in a five-game match in Seoul.
notes: Google blog post dated March 16, 2016: 'The final score was 4-1.' The post does not give the match dates, so the date is recorded at month precision. A public match, not a product, counted as a release under A21. Release kind added by amendment A21: listed because the system is named in at least one statement in data/statements.csv (marcus-2019-01).

title: OpenAI announces GPT-2
description: OpenAI announced GPT-2, a language model trained to predict the next word in 40GB of internet text, at first releasing only a smaller version.
notes: Page dated February 14, 2019: 'Our model, called GPT-2 (a successor to GPT), was trained simply to predict the next word in 40GB of Internet text.' Release kind added by amendment A21: listed because the system is named in at least one statement in data/statements.csv (marcus-2020-01).

title: OpenAI's GPT-3 paper
description: OpenAI introduced GPT-3 in the paper 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners'; public access through OpenAI's API followed on 11 June 2020.
notes: arXiv 2005.14165: 'Submitted on 28 May 2020'. API announcement dated June 11, 2020 (https://openai.com/index/openai-api/), which does not name GPT-3 in its text, so the paper date is used. Release kind added by amendment A21: listed because the system is named in at least one statement in data/statements.csv (altman-2020-01).

title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT
description: OpenAI released ChatGPT, a conversational AI model, as a free research preview.
notes: Page dated November 30, 2022: 'We've trained a model called ChatGPT which interacts in a conversational way.' Release kind added by amendment A21: listed because the system is named in at least one statement in data/statements.csv (hinton-2023-07, as 'ChatGPT4').

title: OpenAI releases GPT-4
description: OpenAI released GPT-4, a large model taking image and text inputs, available through ChatGPT Plus and its API.
notes: Page dated March 14, 2023: 'We've created GPT-4, the latest milestone in OpenAI's effort in scaling up deep learning.' Release kind added by amendment A21: listed because the system is named in at least one statement in data/statements.csv (hinton-2023-04, hinton-2023-07, altman-2023-01, altman-2023-05).

title: DeepSeek releases DeepSeek-R1
description: The Chinese company DeepSeek released DeepSeek-R1, a reasoning model it said performed on par with OpenAI's o1.
notes: Announcement 'DeepSeek-R1 Release', dated January 20, 2025: 'Performance on par with OpenAI-o1'. Release kind added by amendment A21: listed because the system is named in at least one statement in data/statements.csv (lecun-2025-03).

title: OpenAI releases GPT-5
description: OpenAI released GPT-5, which it described as its best AI system yet.
notes: Page dated August 7, 2025: 'We are introducing GPT-5, our best AI system yet.' Release kind added by amendment A21: listed because the system is named in at least one statement in data/statements.csv (marcus-2025-02, altman-2025-07).

title: AI Seoul Summit and Seoul Declaration
description: The second international AI summit, co-hosted by South Korea and the UK in Seoul, ended with world leaders agreeing the Seoul Declaration for safe, innovative and inclusive AI.
notes: gov.uk: 'Published 21 May 2024'; documents 'agreed by world leaders represented at the AI Seoul Summit'. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: A Right to Warn about Advanced Artificial Intelligence
description: Current and former employees of OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Anthropic asked AI companies to let staff raise concerns about risks without retaliation; Yoshua Bengio, Geoffrey Hinton and Stuart Russell endorsed it.
notes: Page dated June 4th, 2024. Key sentence: 'We therefore call upon advanced AI companies to commit to these principles.' About 13 signers, seven named (including Daniel Kokotajlo, Jacob Hilton, William Saunders), six anonymous. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: The EU AI Act enters into force
description: The European Union's law on artificial intelligence entered into force, with its rules applying in stages over the following years.
notes: European Commission news, 1 August 2024: 'On 1 August 2024, the European Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) enters into force.' Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: California governor vetoes SB 1047
description: Governor Gavin Newsom vetoed SB 1047, a bill that would have required developers of the largest AI models to put safeguards in place against catastrophic harm.
notes: Veto message dated SEP 29 2024: 'I am returning Senate Bill 1047 without my signature.' Included as a California action on the largest AI models, where most leading AI companies are based. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: US Executive Order 14179 on AI
description: President Trump signed Executive Order 14179, 'Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence', which ordered a review of actions taken under the revoked Executive Order 14110 and an AI action plan within 180 days.
notes: Federal Register 2025-02172 (90 FR 8741), published 2025-01-31: 'Executive Order 14179 of January 23, 2025'. Sec. 1: 'This order revokes certain existing AI policies and directives that act as barriers to American AI innovation.' EO 14110 itself was revoked on 2025-01-20 (see us-eo-14110-2023). Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: First International AI Safety Report
description: The first International AI Safety Report, written by 96 experts, summarised the evidence on what advanced AI can do and its risks.
notes: arXiv 2501.17805, 'Submitted on 29 January 2025'; Yoshua Bengio listed first of 96 authors. The gov.uk publication page now redirects to https://internationalaisafetyreport.org/. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: Paris AI Action Summit statement
description: The third international AI summit, in Paris, ended with a Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable Artificial Intelligence for People and the Planet, signed by 65 parties.
notes: Elysee page dated 11 February 2025; lists 65 signatories including the European Union and the African Union Commission. The page does not name countries that declined. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: America's AI Action Plan
description: The White House released 'Winning the AI Race: America's AI Action Plan', the plan Executive Order 14179 had called for.
notes: White House article dated July 23, 2025: 'The White House today released "Winning the AI Race: America's AI Action Plan"'. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: California signs SB 53
description: Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, which sets new requirements for developers of frontier AI models.
notes: Governor's office, September 29, 2025: 'SB 53 establishes new requirements for frontier AI developers creating stronger:' (transparency, innovation, safety, accountability). Included as a California law on the largest AI models. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: Statement on Superintelligence
description: The Future of Life Institute released a one-sentence statement calling for a prohibition on developing superintelligence until there is broad scientific agreement it can be done safely and strong public support; signers included Yoshua Bengio, Geoffrey Hinton and Stuart Russell.
notes: Statement: 'We call for a prohibition on the development of superintelligence, not lifted before there is broad scientific consensus that it will be done safely and controllably, and strong public buy-in.' The statement page shows no date; FLI's October 2025 newsletter (https://newsletter.futureoflife.org/p/fli-newsletter-october-2025): 'almost 65,000 signatures on our Statement on Superintelligence, released October 22.' Page count at retrieval (2026-10-08): 77,076. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: US Executive Order 14365 on state AI laws
description: President Trump signed Executive Order 14365, 'Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence', aimed at a single national approach in place of differing state AI laws.
notes: Federal Register 2025-23092 (90 FR 58499), published 2025-12-16: 'Executive Order 14365 of December 11, 2025'. Sec. 1: 'United States AI companies must be free to innovate without cumbersome regulat[ion]' (page text truncated at retrieval). Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: India AI Impact Summit and Declaration
description: The fourth international AI summit, in New Delhi, ended with the India AI Impact Summit Declaration, endorsed by 92 countries and international organisations; 13 frontier AI developers announced the New Delhi Frontier AI Impact Commitments.
notes: Indian government press release posted 02 MAR 2026: summit 'held from 16–21 February 2026'; 'The India AI Impact Summit Declaration was endorsed by 92 countries and international organisations.' The exact day of adoption was not confirmed from a primary source (news reports give 20 or 21 February), so the date is at month precision. The EU endorsement page is dated 20 February 2026 (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/european-union-endorses-leaders-declaration-ai-summit-india). Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: US Executive Order 14409 on advanced AI security
description: President Trump signed Executive Order 14409, 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security', on the national security side of advanced AI.
notes: Federal Register 2026-11415 (91 FR 34565), published 2026-06-05: 'Executive Order 14409 of June 2, 2026'. Sec. 1: 'Advanced AI capabilities make our Nation stronger, but also introduce new national security considerations'. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: Pacing the Frontier
description: More than 1,300 employees of frontier AI companies, including Anthropic's chief executive and OpenAI's chief scientist, asked the US government to support an international effort to build tools that could deliberately slow the pace of automated AI development.
notes: Page headed 'JULY 2026', 'A statement from 1,386 employees of frontier AI companies' (count at retrieval, 2026-10-08). Key sentence: 'We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development.' Named signers include Jakub Pachocki, Jared Kaplan, Shane Legg, Ilya Sutskever, Dario Amodei. News reports date it 28 July 2026; the page gives only the month. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: US Executive Order 14434, 'Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence'
description: President Trump signed Executive Order 14434, directing federal agencies to say 'Super Intelligence' in place of 'Artificial Intelligence' in their communications and asking for a new legal definition.
notes: Federal Register 2026-20321 (91 FR 63129), published 2026-10-02: 'Executive Order 14434 of September 29, 2026'. Sec. 1: 'The capabilities of today's frontier systems do much more than imitate or automate discrete aspects of human intelligence.' What it directs, per a law-firm summary (https://www.wiley.law/alert-Executive-Order-Rebrands-AI-as-Super-Intelligence-and-Signals-Potential-Federal-Legislative-Changes): use 'Super Intelligence' and 'SI' in non-statutory materials, and propose a federal definition. Added under amendment A22 (institutional events since November 2023).

title: Open Letter on AI and Cybersecurity from the Scientific Community
description: Academic researchers (494 signatories at retrieval, over 400 at posting), including Yoshua Bengio and Geoffrey Hinton, called for high-assurance containment and air-gapping of cyber-capable AI models and for an international body to set containment standards and record containment failures, after incidents in which AI models escaped sandboxes and compromised other organisations' systems.
notes: Page headed 'October 2026'; the posting date 2026-10-13 is from organiser David Lie's own post the same day (https://security.csl.toronto.edu/blog/2026/10/13/open-letter-on-ai-and-cybersecurity-posted/: 'went live today'). Drafted by David Lie, Nicolas Papernot and Thomas Ristenpart (University of Toronto and Cornell). Key sentence: 'We, the undersigned scientists, contend that both more AI safety research and more emphasis on containment technologies and procedures are needed.' '494 Signatories' at retrieval 2026-10-16; Bengio and Hinton checked on the page's own list. Appended by the weekly reading of 2026-10-16 (data/readings/2026-10-16.json; searches reading-2026-10-16-34 to -37).
